headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that Dominion Energy Virginia propose tariffs to the State Corporation Commission to allocate certain grid infrastructure costs to large energy users, primarily data centers, rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Congressman Wants States to Make Data Centers Pay Grid Costs or Risk Highway Funds
news_summary: Virginia Rep. Suhas Subramanyam introduced a federal plan requiring utilities to recover full grid upgrade costs from large electricity users, tying implementation to federal highway funding. This initiative aims to address the growing debate over electricity demand, utility costs, and data center development.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This law requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, providing transparency and data for informed decisions on water resources.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public - WHRO
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality. This aims to provide transparency and better information for managing water resources, addressing concerns about the industry's significant water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including noise studies for nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires site assessments for large data centers, including noise studies for homes and schools within 500 feet. However, it mandates studies but does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, leaving some discretion to local officials.
